title: How to Make a Shot List With AI in 5 Steps
summary: Learn how to make a shot list in 5 steps, with a free shot list template and the real shot list behind a scene of Xenogenesis, a residency film made in Flick.
body_markdown:
### What is a shot list?


A shot list is a numbered list of every shot a film or scene needs, in the order it will be shot or played. Each row names the shot's size, camera angle, camera movement and what happens in it, so the director and crew, or an AI model, know exactly what to make.


### What should a shot list include?


At least a shot number, the scene, the shot size, the camera angle, the camera movement and a one-line description of the action and dialogue. Many filmmakers add sound, length, the props and characters each shot needs, and a column to mark the take they keep.


### What is the difference between a shot list and a storyboard?


A shot list describes each shot in words, in a table, while a storyboard draws each shot as a picture. Many productions write the shot list first, since it is faster to change, then storyboard the shots that are hardest to describe.


### How many shots should a scene have?


As many as the scene has beats, the moments where something changes. A short dialogue scene often needs between five and fifteen shots: an establishing or wide shot, close-ups for each speaker, reverse shots for the replies, and inserts for important objects.


### Can AI make a shot list for me?


Yes. An AI chat can break a written scene into numbered shots with sizes, angles and moves in seconds, and in Flick each row can then become a prompt and a generated shot on the same canvas. Read the draft against your own idea of the scene, since the AI does not know which moment matters most.


### Is there a free shot list template?


Yes. A shot list template is a table with the columns shot, scene, size, angle, movement, action and dialogue, sound, length, references and take. Copy those columns into any spreadsheet or document and add one row per shot.


### Who makes the shot list on a film?


The director usually makes the shot list with the director of photography, during pre-production. On a small or solo AI film, the filmmaker writes it alone, often straight from the script, before generating any shots.
